title: Memory flows: geometry and dynamics of sequential retrieval in input-driven Hopfield networks
summary: Associative memory models classically describe retrieval as convergence to stored patterns, but the theory of sequential retrieval remains comparatively limited. We develop a two-timescale input-driven Hopfield network in which fast associative retrieval is modulated by a slow feedback variable evolving over a prescribed memory-transition graph. This yields autonomous, graph-constrained transitions while preserving analytical tractability. Using slow-fast and geometric singular perturbation theory, we characterize memory fixation via memory manifolds and identify the geometric regions that govern stability loss and escape from retrieved memories. We further derive reduced slow dynamics and explicit criteria for transition onset, self-sustained retrieval, and collapse, expressed through escape times, gain thresholds, and fixed points. Together, these results provide a tractable framework for analyzing feedback-driven sequential retrieval in Hopfield networks.

title: How Path Integral Diffusion Decides a Finite Spin Glass
summary: When an AI diffusion-type generator samples a frustrated spin glass, which macroscopic alternatives does it decide first, and when? We study this for bridge-diffusion models of the Path Integral Diffusion (PID) type started from a point source. We show that every isotropic PID is a time-changed Gaussian stochastic localization, and conversely every signal-to-noise schedule is realized by a PID protocol. What a continuous-time generator decides therefore does not depend on the protocol, which only sets when and at what cost. We describe the generator's state by its partial commitments: the probabilities it assigns, at each moment, to nested classes of configurations fixed by the target. The partial commitments are martingales that move only along class contrasts. Their ensemble average gives the information about each level at an exact rate set by squared magnetization contrasts. Each split is decided, approximately, like a binary Gaussian channel at signal-to-noise ratio 1.04/λ_P, with λ_P the leading eigenvalue of the parent's correlation matrix. The theory is applied to Bethe-lattice and Sherrington--Kirkpatrick (SK) glasses with up to 64 spins. It is observed generically that a trajectory first shifts its weight to one of the two mirror halves of the zero-field measure and then to the glassy classes inside it. These classes appear near the glass transition and keep their identity on cooling. Nested glassy levels have similar λ_P and are decided together, so a trajectory commits in one or two distinct events---the mirror choice and a compound glassy decision---which separate further with coupling and size, as the spectra predict. For a generator that takes finitely many steps, the protocol matters through the late, local stage rather than the macroscopic decisions.

title: Spatial effects of Kuramoto modeling on the power-grid frequencies
summary:
Spatial coupling and heterogeneity can generate complex power-grid frequency dynamics. We investigate the contributions of spatial structure, intrinsic nonlinear dynamics, and external driving using the Kuramoto model (KM), with and without uncorrelated noise, and compare its predictions with real-grid measurements.
  We analyse one month of 100 ms frequency measurements from 16 Hungarian transmission-grid sites and simulate the KM on a 387-node transmission network and two-dimensional lattices. The measured power spectra exhibit two scaling regimes, with exponents of approximately 1.63 and 2.23. One-second frequency increments decorrelate rapidly, while correlations of their local inverse variance decay slowly, initially as a power law, $τ^{-0.26(2)}$, up to 15 minutes. A superstatistical Gaussian mixture based on measured local variances captures much of the non-Gaussian increment distribution, but not the rare extreme events.
  We also estimate the non-stationary long-time frequency autocorrelation exponent. KM simulations on low-dimensional networks exhibit algebraically decaying autocorrelations and power spectra, consistent with the measurements and the Wiener-Khinchin relation in the steady state. On the heterogeneous transmission network, partial synchronization and frequency locking produce persistent spatial patterns and multi-peaked frequency distributions. However, neither deterministic KM dynamics nor independent Gaussian driving reproduces the measured spectra and increment statistics simultaneously. Moreover, empirical frequency fluctuations are largely shared across substations, whereas simulated fluctuations mainly reflect relative node motion. These findings suggest that spatially coupled nonlinear dynamics contribute to observed frequency fluctuations alongside external driving, including 15-minute power dispatches.

title: Roadmap on Nanoscale Superconductivity for Quantum Technologies
summary: In 2025, the Year of Quantum Science and Technology, we celebrate a century of quantum mechanics, witnessing a surge in activities that illuminate its inherent strangeness and drive technological innovation. Superconductivity, discovered 114 years ago, stands as a prime example, offering direct and compelling evidence of macroscopic quantum phenomena. Beyond its ability to conduct immense currents without loss, superconductivity reveals the quantum realm operating on a scale we can directly observe and manipulate. The macroscopic quantum coherence, where an ensemble of particles is described by a single wave function, leads to remarkable consequences: dissipation-less current and flux quantization - the basic properties exploited in superconducting quantum circuit fabrication. This Roadmap has been inspired by intensive discussions and collaborations emerging from the European COST Action CA21144 (SuperQuMap - Superconducting Nanodevices and Quantum Materials for Coherent Manipulation). The roadmap outlines the network's concrete activities, driving advancements in superconductor-based quantum technologies and charting future directions. Spanning fundamental research to practical applications, the roadmap incorporates insights from industry partners developing quantum computation. It begins by exploring quantum materials, highlighting how topology and electronic correlations could catalyze a quantum leap in technology. We then delve into manipulating the superconducting phase, leveraging advancements in magnetism, 3D fabrication, and tunable correlations. Further, we showcase the advanced microscopy techniques - such as angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and scanning probes - used to visualize quantum behavior. Finally, and crucially, we detail the quantum devices developed within the network, and their transformative impact on modern quantum computing approaches.

title: Operator-Adapted Multiscale Kernels for High-Contrast Elliptic Inverse Problems
summary:
We consider the joint recovery of the state and diffusion coefficient in a high-contrast elliptic equation from sparse, noisy state measurements. We seek the coefficient in a parameterized family defined relative to a prescribed reference coefficient. We construct a generalized multiscale finite element basis from the reference coefficient and use it to define a finite-rank kernel for the state. A weak Galerkin residual enforces the equation without pointwise differentiation across material interfaces. For each trial coefficient, the state is obtained by solving a linear least-squares problem. Variable projection eliminates the state coordinates from the objective, and the reduced gradient is evaluated without an adjoint PDE solve.
  We split the state reconstruction error into multiscale approximation, penalty relaxation, and parameter estimation terms. Under an admissible patch decomposition, the squared multiscale approximation error is bounded by a local spectral tail estimate with a contrast-independent interpolation constant. For a fixed coefficient and discretization, the penalty relaxation error is of order $O(\varepsilon^2)$ when the residual weight is proportional to $\varepsilon^{-2}$. The parameter contribution is bounded by local Lipschitz continuity of the projected state. In 50 synthetic tests based on a reference medium of contrast $10^4$, the multiscale space with the weak residual gives mean relative state and log-coefficient errors of 2.37\% and 4.43\%, respectively, the lowest among the four configurations tested.

title: A new butterfly in the meadow: magnetic lattice graphs with a circulant vertex coupling
summary: We analyze the spectrum of quantum square lattice graph exposed to a homogeneous magnetic field with a rational flux through plaquette, assuming all nontrivial cases of the vertex coupling which is circulant and scale-invariant, with a particular attention to those of them that give rise to a dynamics violating the time reversal invariance. Except for two cases with partially decoupled edges, the remaining twelve split into two spectral classes; the second one offers a hitherto unknown butterfly pattern.

title: Pelletization Pressure Engineering of the Superconducting Properties of Fluorine-Doped PrFeAsO
summary: We investigate the influence of the pelletization pressure on the structural, microstructural, and superconducting properties of fluorine-doped PrFeAsO0.7F0.3 (Pr1111). Precursor powders are pressed into pellets at pressures ranging from 174 to 1131 MPa, after which the applied pressure is released and all samples undergo an identical two-step conventional synthesis process at ambient pressure (CSP-AP). All samples predominantly exhibit the tetragonal P4/nmm structure, and the lattice parameter a and unit-cell volume V decrease with increasing pelletization pressure up to an intermediate-pressure range (~900 MPa) before increasing at higher pressures. The actual fluorine-content derived from energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) also increase with pelletization pressure, while Raman spectra show only modest variations in the characteristic vibrational modes associated with Fe and As. The superconducting response exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on the pelletization pressure. Among the investigated samples, the sample pelletized at 870 MPa exhibits the most favorable overall superconducting properties, with a superconducting onset temperature of 44.2 K, ~5 K higher than that of the lowest-pressure sample. It also displays a narrower superconducting transition, the highest relative sample density, a favorable effective magnetic critical current density at high fields, and a relatively large effective thermally activated flux-flow activation energy. At higher pelletization pressures, the superconducting response deteriorates, coinciding with increases in the lattice parameters, increased secondary-phase contributions, and reduced relative density. These findings establish the pelletization pressure as a relevant processing parameter for modifying the structural, microstructural and superconducting properties of Pr1111 during CSP-AP.

title: Laplace approximation of the parameter posterior with embedded error for efficient uncertainty quantification of expensive model calibrations
summary: In practical engineering, there is a clear need for uncertainty quantification (UQ) of models used in design because forward UQ puts probabilities on performance predictions. However, without surrogate building, most forward engineering models are too expensive for traditional UQ methods like Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling. Our goal is to provide inexpensive, approxi- mate UQ that can be applied after an expensive traditional least squares fit, where the UQ handles both uncorrelated noise and parameter variance as in the embedded-error treatment developed by Sargsyan, Najm, and Ghanem (2015). After developing the basic theory to connect a Laplace-like approximation to Bayesian calibration, we compare the proposed method to black-box variational inference in terms of cost and fidelity. Then we demonstrate the method on real-world calibration of solid material models.

title: Rayleigh's conjecture in dimensions four and five
summary: We prove Rayleigh's conjecture for the clamped plate in dimensions four and five. In fact, we obtain a sharp comparison with the first Dirichlet eigenvalue: on every open set of finite positive measure, the first plate eigenvalue is at least the square of the Dirichlet eigenvalue multiplied by the ratio attained on a ball. The proof uses a homogeneous transformation of a trial function and its gradient. Two divergence identities reduce the comparison to positivity of a quadratic form in the Hessian. We establish the required Bessel inequalities by rational estimates for entire profiles and their remainders. An exact defect identity accounts for regular nodal sets, so the argument allows trial functions of either sign and imposes no boundary regularity. The domains may be disconnected or unbounded. We characterize equality up to sets of zero Sobolev capacity. We also obtain quantitative stability with the optimal quadratic power of the Fraenkel asymmetry.

title: Mimicry of $\textit{d}$-wave Andreev Signatures by Interlayer Pairing
summary: The recent discovery of high-$T_{\rm c}$ superconductivity in bilayer nickelates has attracted enormous attention. Despite dominant theoretical studies pointing to interlayer pairing, the pairing symmetry is strongly debated due to conflicting evidence on nodeless bulk gaps and $d$-wave-like transport signatures. Here, we demonstrate that a nodeless interlayer pairing can naturally mimic $d$-wave Andreev signatures when the point contact is not evenly coupled to the two layers. The phenomenon can be understood by recognizing how a contact potential, which is odd under the layer-exchanging mirror symmetry, acts like an effective Zeeman field on the layer pseudospin. This pseudo field then binds in-gap Andreev states that sweep through the gap with the width and strength of the barrier. We further demonstrate in a realistic model for La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ that the simulated subgap conductance for a top-layer barrier can reproduce the orientation dependent ZBCP usually interpreted as a fingerprint of $\textit{d}$-wave pairing. By revealing this mirror-selective Andreev response from an interlayer pairing state, our work offers a natural scenario to reconcile the conflicting experimental evidence in bilayer nickelates and advances our understanding of unconventional superconductivity.

title: Convergence of Adaptive Least Squares Finite Element Methods
summary: We consider a general class of operator equations $\mathcal B u=f$ where $\mathcal B:\mathbb U\to \mathbb L_2$ is a linear isomorphis from a Hilbert space $\mathbb U$ onto an ``$L_2$-type'' space $\mathbb L_2 = L_2(Ω;\mathbb R^q)$. This covers weak first order formulations of stationary elliptic boundary value problems, the Stokes system or systems for linear elasticity as well as space-time formulations of heat or wave equations. Since an $L_2$-residual is uniformly equivalent to the corresponding error in the trial space norm reliable and efficient computable a posteriori error bounds are for free. In contrast to a matured theory of classical adaptive finite element methods, estblishing linear convergence - and eventually optimal complexity - in a least squares setting seems to have remained open. To a large extent this is due to the fact that least squares error indicators do not exhibit any explicit dependence on local mesh-sizes. In this paper we propose a rather different approach to establish under which circumstances standard Dörfler-marking mesh refinement gives rise to linear convergence and rate optimality of adaptive least squares finite element methods as well. A central role is played by a new notion of {\em data-visibility} which is a structural property of the data rather than a smoothness condition.

title: Current-voltage characteristics of layered cuprate superconductors with intrinsic Josephson junctions
summary: A brief review of the results for the current-voltage characteristics study in highly anisotropic cuprate superconductors is presented, considering the existence of the intrinsic Josephson effect in multilayer HTSC compounds. We analyzed the observations of multi-branch current-voltage characteristics for current in the c-direction both for the hole-doped and electron-doped cuprate SCs wich conveniently viewed as a strack of intrinsic Josephson junctions, where the CuO2 layers serve as superconducting plates and the buffer layers as dielectric interlayers. It was shown that the tunneling characteristics of intrinsic Josephson junctions in optimally doped p- and n-type cuprates indicate a predominantly d-wave symmetry of the order parameter, demonstrating high conductivity in the subgap regime: U < 2delta/e. The analysis carried out confirms the theoretically predicted power-law dependences U ~ I^gamma with gamma = (0.33 - 0.50) in the hole-doped Bi- and Tl-compounds, which is typical for SCs with monotonic dx^2-y^2 - wave symmetry of the order parameter and with gamma = (0.70 - 0.76) for electron-doped SCs with a non-monotonic d-wave symmetry within the framework of the two-band/two-gap model.

title: How good are spline spaces for the Kolmogorov $n$-width of a Sobolev ball?
summary: This paper studies the approximation power of polynomial splines on a uniform one-dimensional mesh. The quality of the best approximation of the unit ball of $H^{s}$ by an $n$-dimensional subspace, measured in the $L^{2}$ norm, is quantified by the sup-inf of that space: for each function in the Sobolev ball, take its minimal approximation error over the space, and then take the supremum of these errors over the ball. The infimum of this sup-inf over all $n$-dimensional spaces is the well-known Kolmogorov $n$-width $d_{n}$. Choosing the $n$-dimensional subspace to be the piecewise polynomial space of degree $k$ with smoothness $C^μ$ ($-1\leμ\le k-1$) gives our sup-inf $E$. The approximation accuracy of spline spaces is then examined by comparing $d_{n}$ and $E$. The two quantities are determined by two eigenvalue problems, through which we obtain a lower bound for $d_{n}$ and an upper bound for $E$. Under the restriction $k\ge s-1$, the upper bound for the error of the maximally smooth spline space ($μ=k-1$) is asymptotically equal to the lower bound for $d_n$, showing that uniform $B$-splines are asymptotically optimal among all $n$-dimensional spaces. For $μ<k-1$, we prove that $E/d_n$ is bounded below by a constant strictly larger than $1$, except when $k>s-1$ and $μ=k-2$ hold simultaneously. This reveals the superiority of $B$-splines in the sense of $n$-widths. Numerical experiments corroborate these bounds and, in some cases (e.g. the exception above), show that they are sharp.

title: Transverse quasiparticle heat transport in p-wave magnetic Josephson junctions
summary: We study transverse heat currents carried by Bogoliubov quasiparticles in $p$-wave magnetic Josephson junctions under a longitudinal temperature bias. We find that such a junction supports a transverse spin heat current while the net transverse heat current vanishes. This effect stems from the $p$-wave magnetism, which shifts the two spin sectors oppositely in transverse momentum space and thereby causes them to carry opposite heat currents. A weak Zeeman field lifts the compensation between the two spin-sector contributions, thereby generating a finite net transverse heat current. The directions of both currents can be switched by reversing the sign of the $p$-wave magnetic splitting or tuning the superconducting phase difference, while both currents vanish in the absence of $p$-wave magnetism. These findings highlight $p$-wave magnetic Josephson junctions as a versatile platform for switchable transverse heat transport and controllable spin caloritronics.

title: High-order long-time stable methods for the forced incompressible Navier--Stokes equations
summary: We present in this paper two scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) correction steps for constructing long-time stable schemes for the forced incompressible Navier--Stokes equations with no-slip boundary conditions. A main feature is that the same correction steps apply to any linear predictor satisfying the order and spatial regularity requirements in Assumption~P. Their construction and stability analysis are independent of the particular form of the predictor and require no energy estimate for it. The first correction uses a damped, shifted kinetic-energy variable to obtain a uniform-in-time $L^2$ bound in two and three dimensions, together with a weighted dissipation estimate. In two dimensions, the second correction combines a higher-energy auxiliary variable with a scalar relaxation to yield a uniform-in-time $H^1$ bound. Under the stated assumptions, these estimates hold on arbitrary positive time grids, without restrictions on step sizes or adjacent step ratios. We also derive eventual absorbing bounds; for the two-SAV scheme, these apply to the admissible initial class associated with fixed parameters. The generalized BDF schemes require one constant-coefficient Helmholtz solve per velocity component and one pressure Poisson solve per step; the second correction adds no field solve. Numerical experiments exhibit second-, third-, and fourth-order convergence for the tested BDF schemes and illustrate the long-time stability and efficiency of adaptive time stepping.

title: Pseudogap in hole doped cuprates: a status report
summary: The pseudogap state, an anomalous momentum dependent partial suppression of low energy electronic excitations persisting well above the superconducting critical temperature in underdoped cuprates, remains one of the most profound enigmas in condensed physics today. This review summarizes over three decades of experimental and theoretical progress. It appears that pseudogap is not a mere precursor to superconductivity, but a distinct, intertwined state of matter characterized by a complex interplay of competing and cooperating electronic orders. We critically examine the bulk probes like resistivity and magnetic susceptibility and the surface hallmark spectroscopic signatures observed via angle resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) in this review. ARPES reveals a Fermi surface truncated into disconnected segments and scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) visualizes a spatially heterogeneous energy gap around the Fermi level. These observations are contextualized alongside transport anomalies, including resistivity and bulk magnetic susceptibility, to construct a phenomenological portrait of a phase that violates conventional Fermi liquid theory. By mapping the electronic phase diagram, we highlight the abrupt transition at above optimal doping. We conclude with open questions still to be answered. This review underscores the role of the pseudogap as a key to unlocking the unconventional pairing mechanism of hole doped cuprates and the broader physics of strongly correlated electron systems.

title: A Trajectory-Aware Domain-Decomposed Multispace Reduced Basis Preconditioner for Parametric Helmholtz Problems
summary: Repeated solutions of parametric Helmholtz problems arise in multi-query applications such as sensitivity analysis and uncertainty quantification. Classical preconditioned iterative solvers do not automatically reuse low-dimensional structures across parameters. Multispace reduced basis (MSRB) preconditioners can exploit such structures by constructing iteration-specific reduced order models (ROMs) from training data, but storing global iteration-dependent bases incurs substantial memory costs. Building on trajectory-aware MSRB training, we develop a domain-decomposed MSRB (DD-MSRB) preconditioner for parametric Helmholtz systems truncated by perfectly matched layers (PMLs). Within flexible GMRES, each reduced space is trained on inverse-action snapshots along the Krylov trajectories generated by the ROM-based preconditioners applied in preceding iterations. To reduce storage, problem-adapted spatial partitions exploit heterogeneous local snapshot compressibility across the physical interior and the PML. Local basis dimensions in each subdomain are determined greedily under a global snapshot-error budget to balance approximation accuracy and storage. The resulting hybrid solver applies DD-MSRB preconditioning during the initial iterations to capture dominant cross-parameter modes and then switches, when necessary, to a shifted-Laplacian preconditioner to reduce error components poorly represented by the reduced spaces. Numerical experiments on two-dimensional half-space propagation, elliptic-obstacle scattering, and three-dimensional waveguides demonstrate significant acceleration over the shifted-Laplacian baseline and substantial memory savings relative to global MSRB. For the largest waveguide system, with 11.0 million unknowns, DD-MSRB reduces deployed ROM storage by 44.9% and mean online solve time by 30.2% compared with global MSRB.

title: Ferromagnetic resonance signatures of edge states for distinguishing chiral and helical $p$-wave superconductors
summary: We theoretically investigate ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) modulation at interfaces between ferromagnetic insulators and two-dimensional chiral and helical $p$-wave superconductors. We evaluate the surface dynamical spin susceptibility, including both edge and bulk quasiparticle excitations. For momentum-conserving interfacial exchange at zero temperature, the edge contribution to the Gilbert damping exhibits distinct frequency scalings for the excitation energies well above the spectral broadening, $\hbarω\gg2δ$: $δ/(\hbarω)^{2}$ for the chiral state and $1/\hbarω$ for the helical state. For a clean superconducting boundary, edge-induced Ising spin anisotropy persists even when interfacial exchange disorder randomizes momentum transfer. The low-energy edge response is suppressed when the magnetization aligns with the edge-state spin axis. These results establish FMR modulation as a probe complementary to existing methods for distinguishing the chiral and helical states and constraining their $d$-vector directions.

title: Error Estimates and Convergence Analysis for Learning Mechanism--AI Coupled Dynamical Systems
summary: Mechanism--AI coupled dynamical systems retain known mechanisms while learning unknown dynamics from data. We study how neural approximation, numerical integration, finite observations, and optimization jointly affect the accuracy of this learning process. For time-dependent learned terms in a fixed compact admissible class, we derive a four-component objective error bound within an optimal control formulation. Explicit estimates are obtained for constrained ReLU approximation and Euler integration, with deterministic quadrature and random sampling treated separately. Under joint refinement, we establish $Γ$-convergence of the approximate objectives and show that approximate minimizers approach the continuous optimal set when the global optimization gaps vanish. We also derive conditional stability estimates for state-dependent learned terms. Numerical experiments with a susceptible--infected--recovered (SIR) model illustrate the analysis and show how solver resolution affects continuous-trajectory accuracy even when training losses are similar.

title: Identifying Contributions to the Superconducting Diode Effect through Nonreciprocal Superconducting Properties
summary: Nonreciprocal superconducting responses provide a sensitive probe of superconducting states in systems where inversion and time-reversal symmetries are broken. However, in the superconducting diode effect (SDE), where the critical current differs for opposite current directions, nonreciprocity can also arise from vortex-induced contributions caused by minute magnetic field misalignment, complicating its interpretation. Here, we investigate a noncentrosymmetric $[Nb/V/Ta]_{40}$ superlattice and demonstrate nonreciprocity in all three fundamental superconducting properties: the critical current, critical field, and superconducting transition temperature. By measuring the angular dependence of the nonreciprocal critical field $ΔB_{\mathrm{c} 2}$, we separate the contribution of misalignment-induced out-of-plane vortices from the in-plane response. We identify a sharply enhanced SDE emerging near $B_{\mathrm{c} 2}$, accompanied by nonreciprocal responses in $T_{\mathrm{c}}$. These observations exhibit phenomenology similar to that reported in layered superconductors, where an orbital-FFLO state with finite-momentum Cooper pairing has been reported. Our results establish a protocol for assessing out-of-plane vortex contributions to the superconducting diode effect and demonstrate that nonreciprocal responses provide complementary probes of unconventional superconducting states.

title: A high-order structure-preserving ALE--SAV finite element method for moving contact line flows
summary: We develop a structure-preserving arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian (ALE) finite element method for incompressible Navier--Stokes flow with gravity and moving contact lines, based on a scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) reformulation. The reformulation expresses the geometric energy quadratically in the auxiliary variable and permits linear treatment of the capillary, wetting and gravitational forces. The method combines high-order isoparametric elements in space with a linearly implicit, second-order Crank--Nicolson discretization in time. Second-order extrapolation supplies the predicted geometry and known coefficients of the linear fluid--SAV system. Mesh motion changes the kinetic-energy inner product and requires a compatible discretization of the time-derivative terms in the ALE formulation. We discretize these terms using an $L^2$-isometric velocity transfer to retain the kinetic-energy balance after the geometry update. We also construct a boundary update that preserves area or volume exactly using only linear solves. The resulting scheme satisfies a discrete SAV energy-dissipation law and preserves area or volume exactly. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions demonstrate high-order spatial and second-order temporal convergence and confirm SAV energy dissipation and area or volume conservation.

title: Sub-Thouless energy scale in interface-dominated unconventional superconductor junctions
summary: We derive the conductance in unconventional superconductor - normal metal - normal metal junctions, taking into account the resistance between the normal metals. We show that applying Tanaka--Nazarov boundary conditions at both superconductor and normal metal interfaces reveals a new characteristic low-energy scale which is sub-Thouless in the experimentally relevant strong-interface regime. This scale governs, among other quantities, the curvature of the local density of states (LDOS) and the width of conductance dips near the zero-bias conductance peak in triplet superconductor junctions, thereby replacing the Thouless energy as the dominant low-energy parameter. We derive universal $s$-wave proximitized diffusive metal expressions for the zero-bias LDOS and differential conductance which solely depend on the interface and bulk resistances, independent of the superconducting gap and Thouless energy scale. This framework provides a possible origin of the anomalous low-bias conductance features observed in unconventional superconductors, offering a refined mechanism for interpreting interface and correlated electron physics in experimental hybrid junctions.

title: Neural Operator Surrogates for Landweber Iteration in Solving Inverse Problems
summary: Neural operators can accurately approximate well-posed mappings, but for unbounded or discontinuous operators, common in inverse problems, we verify that their network parameters often blow up in architectures such as DeepONet and FNO. To solve inverse problems stably, we use Landweber iteration, which requires only a forward map and the adjoint of its derivative (linearisation). To reduce repeated PDE forward evaluations, we replace the forward operator and its derivative with a differentiable neural-operator surrogate. We show that encoder-network-decoder operators, including generalised DeepONets and fully coupled Fourier operators, approximate both the forward map and its derivative. A modified discrepancy principle ensures decreasing error before finite stopping. With a compact preconditioner, the iterates remain in a compact set where accurate surrogates exist, and the stopped reconstructions converge as data and surrogate errors vanish under a regularity condition. We also relate the theory to derivative-informed training along finite directions, showing that the preconditioner determines which derivative errors affect the Landweber iteration update. Experiments on identifying a reaction coefficient in an elliptic equation show that smoothing reduces late-iteration deterioration for less accurate surrogates but slows sharp-feature recovery, and that smaller derivative errors along training directions do not by themselves improve reconstruction accuracy.

title: Multilayer Heater Nano cryotrons: Electrothermal Modeling of Geometry-Dependent Switching
summary: This paper presents a finite-element framework to study how device geometry affects the switching current of multilayer heater nano cryotrons (hTrons). The device comprises a 50 nm Au/5 nm Ti heater, a 100 nm SiO2 spacer, a 23.6 nm NbN channel, and a Si substrate. Two-dimensional electrothermal simulations examine nine heater and channel width combinations using widths of 100, 500, and 1000 nm. Three-dimensional simulations show how heat flows through the layers and spreads across the channel near the heater-channel overlap. Heater electrical losses and heat transport are coupled, whereas the channel switching threshold is obtained separately from a temperature-dependent constitutive relation. Published global temperature measurements support the switching-law calibration, and heater-current measurements assess the resulting device response. The model measurement comparisons show a systematic reduction of switching-current density with heating, but also geometry-dependent discrepancies in the low-drive plateau and transition shape. A common extraction protocol is formulated for heater-current and heater-power requirements at a specified suppression level, while separating fitted device amplitudes from controlled geometry effects. The resulting comparisons connect thermal fields to design metrics while distinguishing calibration from validation and excluding transient-performance claims from the stationary analysis

title: DMP-Oriented Anisotropic Mesh Adaptation for SUPG Finite Element Methods for Time-Dependent Convection-Diffusion Problems
summary: We study discrete bound preservation for fully discrete piecewise-linear streamline upwind Petrov--Galerkin (SUPG) finite element approximations of time-dependent convection--diffusion equations on anisotropic triangular meshes. Although the continuous homogeneous-source problem satisfies a parabolic maximum principle, SUPG approximations can exhibit nonphysical undershoots and overshoots. We derive sufficient nodal discrete maximum principle (DMP) conditions that account for the stabilized mass matrix, the combined effects of physical and streamline diffusion, time-step restrictions, and transfer between successive meshes. The analysis identifies a SUPG-effective diffusion tensor and motivates an anisotropic metric aligned with its inverse. We construct a combined metric that retains the effective-tensor geometry while introducing solution-dependent mesh density through recovered Hessian information. The resulting DMP conditions provide a theoretical basis for anisotropic mesh design. Numerical experiments for time-dependent transport problems with isotropic and moderately anisotropic diffusion demonstrate that, under mass-compatible limited SUPG stabilization, the combined metric substantially reduces measured undershoots relative to other methods at matched nominal mesh budgets, although improved bound behavior can carry an accuracy penalty. A controlled tensor--density comparison in the anisotropic transport test supports a contribution from the effective tensor beyond the prescribed mesh density.

title: Superconductivity and Polar Metallicity in Atomically Thin Nitride Superlattices
summary: The integration of polar and superconducting materials in the atomically thin limit typically results in a competition that suppresses the superconducting order. Here, we challenge this conventional view by employing first-principles calculations to investigate 1:1 superlattices composed of alternating atomically thin layers of TiN/AlN and δ-NbN/AlN. Contrary to the expectation that dense insulating barriers would quench superconductivity, we find that the polar interface can coexist with a superconducting state. We observe that the transition temperature (Tc) of TiN is enhanced by nearly 2 K over its bulk value, while δ-NbN maintains a relatively high Tc exceeding 20 K. We demonstrate that this resilience arises from the formation of a polar metal, where the strong internal electric fields of the AlN layers are partially screened by a charge redistribution within the nitride layers. This screening mechanism, along with the geometric confinement, creates a quasi-two-dimensional electronic environment, establishing these superlattices as a novel platform for exploring the coexistence of structural inversion-symmetry breaking and superconductivity in the two-dimensional limit.

title: On-the-Fly Reduced Bases Through the Lens of Augmented Krylov Methods
summary: On-the-fly reduced order models (ROMs) are widely used in applications where multiple queries of large-scale models are required in an iterative method, like PDE-constrained optimization or fluid-structure interaction. When compared to classical offline--online ROMs, they have the advantage of being agnostic to any precomputed training data, mesh or geometry, which makes them more general linear/nonlinear solver accelerators. The main goal of this work is to study the effect of using a reduced basis constructed on-the-fly to accelerate a restarted Krylov algorithm, and to formally bridge this category of data-driven methods with classical augmented Krylov methods. The guiding principles of on-the-fly reduced basis will be translated into the framework of Krylov subspace methods, for a Petrov-Galerkin projection method. Previous corrections generated by the algorithm are stored in a snapshot matrix, and a singular value decomposition (SVD) is used to determine a reduced subspace containing the most significant directions. It will be shown that this approach can be embedded in the framework of Krylov methods with augmented or deflated restart, but with a different, data-driven recycling strategy. An analytical study will be presented to determine the consequences of augmentation by ROM-based vectors. Numerical experiments on a convection-diffusion problem with various degrees of convection will show that the proposed methodology yields results comparable to classical iterative linear solvers in some regimes, especially for nearly symmetric or skew-symmetric operators. At equal sizes of the augmentation basis, the convergence was sometimes faster with the proposed framework than with deflation methods.

title: Visualizing d-wave pairing symmetry at the atomic scale in a cuprate high-Tc superconductor by Josephson tunneling
summary: Superconducting pairing symmetry provides crucial insight into the microscopic mechanisms of Cooper pairing. However, probing the local manifestations of sign-changing superconducting order parameters remains experimentally challenging. Here, we investigate the superconducting condensate in optimally doped (OPT) Bi2Sr2Ca2Cu3O10+δ (Bi-2223) using scanning Josephson tunneling microscopy (SJTM), equipped with an s-wave superconducting tip. Measurements at ultra-low temperatures reveal a pronounced modulation of the Josephson tunneling signal at different locations inside the crystallographic unit cell. A distinct Josephson tunneling signal is detected above O sites in the underlying CuO2 plane, whereas the signal nearly vanishes above the Cu-plaquette diagonals, including Cu sites and plaquette centers. This unique intra-unit-cell spatial pattern agrees with the theoretical prediction for the symmetry-dependent cancellation of Josephson tunneling between an s-wave superconducting tip and a d-wave superconducting sample. Our findings provide atomic-scale, real-space evidence for d-wave pairing symmetry in OPT high-Tc Bi-2223 and establish SJTM as a powerful approach for investigating the pairing symmetry of unconventional superconductors.

title: An Arbitrary-Order Distributional Finite Element Method for the Curl--Dev Grad Stokes System
summary: We develop an arbitrary-order distributional finite element method for the three-dimensional curl--dev grad Stokes system governed by the Hessian complex. On tetrahedral meshes, the method couples degree-$(k+1)$ nonconforming symmetric-tensor virtual elements, degree-$k$ tangential-normal continuous traceless tensor elements, and Raviart--Thomas elements of index $k$, without additional virtual-element stabilization. Building on zero-extension curl--div theory, we derive a well-posed distributional saddle-point formulation with an $H(\operatorname{div})$ vector multiplier. A divergence-augmented discrete norm equivalence controls the full Raviart--Thomas space modulo translations and underpins mesh-uniform stability for each fixed $k\ge0$. We establish optimal $O(h^{k+1})$ energy error estimates and an optimal $O(h^{k+2})$ $L^2$ error estimate for the full symmetric-tensor approximation, under suitable regularity and load approximation assumptions. As an application, the method supplies the Stokes block of a decoupled triharmonic scheme with optimal Hessian error estimates. Numerical experiments support the predicted convergence rates for computable quantities.

title: Supercurrent-controlled magnon transport via suppression of the superconducting gap
comment: 10 pages, 9 figures, Accepted for publication in Physical Review Applied
summary: Understanding interactions between different low-energy excitations is a central theme in condensed-matter physics. Magnons and superconducting condensates represent two distinct macroscopic quantum states, yet their mutual interaction remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate supercurrent-controlled magnon transport in a ferromagnet/superconductor heterostructure. We observe that the magnon transport signal decreases as the supercurrent increases. This suppression originates from a supercurrent-induced reduction of the superconducting gap, which enhances magnon dissipation into the superconductor via Bogoliubov quasiparticles. Our results provide direct experimental evidence of a supercurrent-controlled interaction between magnons and quasiparticles in the superconductor. The approach used in this study relies on supercurrents, enabling magnon modulation without Joule heating. These findings establish a new route to control magnons via superconductivity and pave the way for energy-efficient magnonic devices.

title: A Discrete de Rham method for linear and nonlinear fourth-order plate models
summary: We develop and analyze a Discrete de Rham (DDR) method for the Kirchhoff--Love plate problem on general polygonal meshes and demonstrate its extension to geometrically nonlinear plates. The construction uses local degrees of freedom and polynomial reconstructions, avoiding the implementation difficulties associated with globally $C^1$-conforming approximation spaces. A new deflection reconstruction obtained from the discrete Hessian permits a uniform treatment of the load term at all polynomial degrees. The use of this reconstruction improves the convergence rates of previous DDR methods and enables the formulation of a lowest-order scheme with only vertex unknowns. We provide a stability and convergence analysis of the method and validate the theoretical results through a comprehensive set of numerical tests. The method is then extended to the coupled von Kármán equations, for which we demonstrate convergence numerically. We also study the flat-branch spectrum of a compressed perforated plate and its small-amplitude forced nonlinear response near the first critical load.

title: Magnetotropic signatures of Fulde-Ferrell Pairing in a Pauli-limited superconductor
summary: Resonant torsion magnetometry measures the angular curvature of the free energy and is sensitive to magnetic anisotropy. We calculate its response for a clean Pauli-limited superconductor with single-plane-wave Fulde-Ferrell pairing. Field rotation drives a first-order transition from the uniform condensate into the finite-momentum phase and a continuous transition into the normal state. The first-order line produces a sharp softening whose integrated weight is fixed by the magnetization jump, so the dip alone does not identify finite momentum. The distinguishing response is a broad softening inside the Fulde-Ferrell phase, caused by relaxation of the gap and pairing momentum, followed by a finite step at the upper critical field.

title: A Geometry-Robust Nečas-Type Inequality for Stokes Preconditioning
summary: Pressure mass preconditioners for the incompressible Stokes equations can deteriorate on domains with narrow gaps. We develop a pressure preconditioner that uses the distance to the boundary to account for spatially varying geometric scales. Its application consists of a pressure mass solve and a weighted pressure Poisson solve, with the squared boundary distance as the diffusion coefficient. The theoretical basis is a distance-weighted pressure norm defined by splitting the pressure into an $L^2$ component and a component controlled by its weighted gradient. We prove that this norm is bounded by the negative norm of the pressure gradient on every bounded connected open set, with a constant depending only on the dimension. A reverse bound follows from the boundary Hardy inequality, giving norm equivalence uniformly over families with bounded Hardy constants. Two-dimensional finite element experiments on slender, perforated, and composite domains demonstrate stable performance across the tested geometric parameters and mesh refinements. The smallest eigenvalues of the preconditioned pressure Schur complement remain close to $0.54$, and block preconditioning with algebraic multigrid auxiliary solves requires about 20--30 FGMRES iterations across the geometric sweeps.

title: Connate Topological Superconductivity and Vortex-Position-Controlled Majorana Modes in the Intergrowth Superconductor Th$_2$Mo$_2$Ir$_2$Si$_4$C
comment: 7 pages, 4 figures; Supplemental Material included (19 pages, 14 figures)
summary: The recently synthesized intergrowth compound Th$_2$Mo$_2$Ir$_2$Si$_4$C is an experimentally established bulk superconductor whose topological electronic structure remains unexplored. Here, we identify it as a candidate for connate topological superconductivity and reveal two microscopic routes to vortex Majorana zero modes. First-principles and tight-binding-model calculations uncover Mo--Th band inversion and helical surface states enabled by interorbital spin--orbit coupling between Mo--d$_{xz/yz}$ and Th--d$_{x^2-y^2}$ orbitals. Vortex Bogoliubov--de Gennes calculations further establish a relatively robust surface-state-associated Kitaev phase and a weakly gapped, Th-orbital-derived Kitaev phase. For the latter, shifting the vortex core closes and reopens the vortex-line gap and reverses its one-dimensional topological invariant, consistent with an effective Kitaev-chain mass inversion. Finite-length-vortex calculations reveal distinct spatial and spin-resolved signatures of their Majorana end modes. The orbital Kitaev phase can also exist without helical surface states in a modified model. Although the small orbital-derived gap limits quantitative predictions of experimental observability in this compound, the uncovered mechanism suggests a route to Majorana vortices in multiorbital superconductors beyond the conventional surface-state scenario.

title: A DG method for the pseudostress-velocity formulation of the Stokes-Brinkman eigenvalue problem
summary: We introduce a discontinuous Galerkin method for the approximation of the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the Stokes-Brinkman eigenvalue problem. The method is based on a mixed formulation in which the pseudostress tensor and the fluid velocity are the main unknowns, while the pressure can be recovered through a post-processing procedure applied to the pseudostress tensor. Using discontinuous polynomial spaces of degree $k\geq 1$, we propose a consistent symmetric interior penalty discretization for the approximation of the spectrum. Relying on the spectral theory for non-compact operators, we establish convergence of the discrete spectral approximation and derive error estimates for the method. A series of numerical experiments is presented to assess its computational performance. On the one hand, we investigate the convergence rates for different polynomial degrees, computational domains, and values of the permeability. Furthermore, we study the influence of the stabilization parameter on the discrete spectrum by comparing different choices of this parameter and examining their impact on the occurrence of spurious eigenvalues.

title: Quantum-geometry-controlled pseudogap and non-Fermi-liquid behavior
summary: The quantum metric plays an essential role in flat-band superconductivity, governing the superfluid weight and coherence length. While previous studies have primarily focused on mean-field superconducting properties, the role of quantum geometry in fluctuation phenomena remains largely unexplored, despite the importance of fluctuations in flat-band systems. To address this issue, we employ a multiorbital T-matrix approximation that retains the orbital structure of the Bloch wave functions. By analyzing models in which the quantum metric can be tuned independently of the band dispersion, we show that an enhanced quantum metric suppresses the fluctuation-induced pseudogap in both flat-band and dispersive-band systems. In dispersive-band systems, this suppression is accompanied by a crossover from non-Fermi-liquid to Fermi-liquid behavior. This spectral evolution suggests a quantum-metric-driven crossover from a BEC-like strong-coupling regime to a BCS-like weak-coupling regime. More broadly, our results establish the quantum metric as a control parameter of interaction-driven fluctuation phenomena beyond mean-field theory.

title: A Legendre-Galerkin Method for Kinetic Models of Opinion Dynamics with Quasi-Invariant Consistency
summary: Kinetic models of opinion dynamics provide a mesoscopic framework for describing collective behavior arising from interactions among a large number of individuals. Highly accurate numerical approximation to such Boltzmann-type equations, however, remains challenging due to the nonlinear inelastic collision operators involving multiple integrals coupling opinion variables and random perturbations. To address the difficulties, we develop a Legendre-Galerkin spectral method for a general class of kinetic models with opinion-dependent interaction rules. Our method exploits an exact decoupling of the weak collision kernel to obtain a time-independent tensor representation of the Galerkin collision operator. A recursive construction reduces collision-tensor assembly to one-dimensional quadrature, allowing the coefficients to be precomputed for subsequent use. A rigorous $L^2$-error estimate, along with mass preservation, is established for the fully discrete scheme under suitable regularity and stability assumptions. In the quasi-invariant regime, we derive the limiting Fokker-Planck equation and establish consistency between the exact Legendre-Galerkin operators of the rescaled Boltzmann equation and its limit for each fixed polynomial degree. Numerical experiments support the theoretical results, illustrate quasi-invariant consistency, and capture the formation of opinion clusters under the bounded-confidence interactions.

title: Real Topology on Symmetry-Invariant Loops Enforces Superconducting Pairing Zeros
summary: Normal-state topology can obstruct superconducting pairing and give rise to gapless nodes in the quasiparticle spectrum. However, existing pairing-obstruction mechanisms largely rely on Fermi-surface topology or global Bloch-band topology. Here, we establish a new and general mechanism: one-dimensional (1D) real topology, defined on antiunitary-symmetry-invariant loops, enforces pairing zeros without requiring Fermi-surface or global Bloch-band topology. We derive sufficient conditions and lower bounds for pairing zeros across diverse pairing channels, for both zero and finite Cooper-pair momenta. The theorems apply to systems of arbitrary spatial dimensions without requiring the pairing bands to be globally isolated. We further show that such topologically enforced pairing zeros, if isolated, necessarily carry odd vorticity and can give rise to Bogoliubov-de Gennes nodes and zero-energy boundary modes, as demonstrated in a minimal two-orbital model. Our results reshape the understanding of how normal-state topology can obstruct the superconducting order, highlight the significant role of 1D real topology beyond single-particle band phenomena, and provide a general framework for identifying candidate materials hosting nodal superconductivity.

title: Suboptimality of Gaussian quadrature for Freud and logistic weights in weighted Sobolev spaces
summary:
We study the worst-case error of Gaussian quadrature for integrals over the real line weighted by Freud weights $\exp(-|x|^β)$ with $β>1$, and by the logistic density $\mathrm{e}^{-x}/(1+\mathrm{e}^{-x})^2$. The integrand functions are assumed to live in the $ρ$-weighted $L^2$-based Sobolev space of smoothness $α\in\mathbb{N}$.
  We prove that any linear quadrature using the $n$ Gaussian nodes, irrespective of the choice of quadrature weights, has a worst-case error bounded from below by a constant times $n^{-α(1-1/β)}$ for the Freud weights, and by a constant times $(\log n)^{-α}$ for the logistic weight. Our proof is based on three simple observations. First, the worst-case error of any linear quadrature is bounded from below in terms of the number of its nodes in a fixed interval. Second, the number of Gaussian nodes in such an interval is bounded from above by means of Christoffel functions. Third, Christoffel functions admit sharp lower bounds on such an interval. For the Freud weights with even integer exponents and for the logistic weight, all steps are proved in an elementary and self-contained way; for the logistic weight, we use explicit recurrence coefficients of the corresponding orthogonal polynomials. Our results provide a theoretical explanation, for integrands of finite smoothness, of the slow convergence of Gauss--Logistic quadrature observed in the literature. In contrast, for the logistic weight and for the Freud weights with even integer exponents, the Möbius-transformed trapezoidal rule attains the optimal rate $n^{-α}$. This rule does not depend on the smoothness $α$ and requires only point values of the integrand and the weight.

title: Scalable operating currents in amorphous W-N/FePt superconducting rectifiers
comment: 10 pages, 7 figures, 1 table. S. Russo and A. Sanson contributed equally to this work
summary: We demonstrate high-efficiency, field-free superconducting diode behavior in W-N/FePt bilayers fabricated entirely by sputtering at room temperature. The devices combine amorphous W-N superconducting thin films with a 48-nm-thick FePt layer exhibiting remanent stripe-domain magnetization. We used lithographically patterned microbridges to compare W-N/FePt bilayers with single-layer W-N reference films at three nominal W-N thicknesses (18, 24, and 28 nm). The bilayers exhibit superconducting transition temperatures of approximately 4.1-4.3 K. At zero applied magnetic field, the current-voltage (I-V) characteristics exhibit pronounced nonreciprocity, controlled by the orientation of the in-plane remanent FePt magnetization relative to the transport current. The diode response is maximized for perpendicular alignment, reverses polarity upon magnetization reversal, and is strongly suppressed when the magnetization is aligned with the current. This behavior is consistent with asymmetric vortex entry and motion governed by the magnetic stray fields generated near the bridge edges. At 3 K with the remanent magnetization perpendicular to the current, increasing the W-N thickness from 18 to 28 nm widens the current interval between the dissipation thresholds for opposite polarities from about 0.3 to 1.55 mA. All three bilayers exhibit diode efficiencies of approximately 75-80% in this configuration.

title: Optimal adaptive finite element methods in $W^{1,p}$
summary: We prove linear convergence and algebraic rate optimality of an adaptive finite element method for the Dirichlet Poisson problem in W1p. We assume well-posedness of the continuous problem and discrete inf-sup stability over the refinement family. We verify both hypotheses when p is sufficiently close to 2, without requiring convexity of the domain. The Galerkin equations remain unchanged, while the residual estimator and Dörfler marking use the target exponent p. Linear convergence holds for every fixed marking fraction between zero and one. For sufficiently small marking fractions and marked sets of nearly minimal cardinality, the method attains the best algebraic rates for W1p approximation together with data oscillation. The main ingredient is a Banach-space extension of Feischl's relaxed quasi-orthogonality, proved under discrete inf-sup stability.

title: Direct imaging of vortex lattices across fractional fillings in two-dimensional Josephson junction arrays
comment: 7 pages, 4 figures, with Supplemental Material. Comments are welcome
summary: Josephson junction arrays are predicted to host a rich sequence of commensurate vortex lattices. However, direct imaging of these configurations remains limited, while transport measurements cannot resolve the underlying vortex arrangements or how order breaks down. Using scanning superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) microscopy, we resolve individual vortices and directly image this long-predicted hierarchy spanning filling factors $f$ = 1/8 to 1/2 in two-dimensional Au-Nb Josephson junction arrays, including several states with no discernible transport signatures. At $f$ = 1/4, two structurally distinct vortex orders with 4$\times$4 and 2$\times$4 unit cells coexist, consistent with their energetic degeneracy in the frustrated XY model. Away from commensurate filling, we resolve defect structures tied to the underlying vortex-lattice order: the $f$ = 1/2 checkerboard retains its order around isolated excess vortices and vacancies, whereas the $f$ = 1/3 staircase fragments into domains separated by domain walls. These results reveal how frustration, competing configurations, and defects shape the spatial coherence of commensurate vortex order in engineered superconducting lattices.

title: An asymptotic preserving scheme for kinetic equations describing bacterial traveling pulses
summary: We consider a kinetic model for bacterial chemotaxis that describes the propagation of traveling pulses driven by a nutrient and a self-produced chemoattractant. In the diffusive regime, the model converges to a macroscopic drift-diffusion system with bounded chemotactic fluxes. We construct a fully discrete asymptotic preserving (AP) finite difference scheme based on a micro-macro decomposition of the kinetic equation. The method is stable uniformly with respect to the scaling parameter and, as this parameter tends to zero, reduces to a consistent discretization of the limiting macroscopic equations. We prove positivity and mass conservation for the limiting scheme, and use a positivity-preserving correction for the kinetic solver. Numerical simulations reproduce the experimentally observed traveling pulses at both the kinetic and the macroscopic level, validate the theoretical traveling wave speed, and illustrate the convergence of the kinetic model to its macroscopic limit.

title: Ambient-pressure superconductivity in bulk single crystals of La$_5$Ni$_4$O$_{10}$
summary: Superconductivity in the Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) nickelates has so far been confined either to multilayer compounds under high pressure or to square-planar infinite-layer-type films stabilized by epitaxial strain. Here we report the high-pressure high-temperature (HPHT) growth of bulk single crystals of the quadruple-layer RP nickelate La$_5$Ni$_4$O$_{13}$ ($n=4$) and reproduce the quintuple-layer La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{16}$ ($n=5$) synthesis, two members of the series that had previously been accessible only as thin films. Topotactic reduction of La$_5$Ni$_4$O$_{13}$ single crystals with CaH$_2$ yields the square-planar phase La$_5$Ni$_4$O$_{10}$, which we show to be a bulk, ambient-pressure superconductor with $T_\mathrm{c}^\mathrm{onset} \approx 18\,\mathrm{K}$, a shielding fraction above 60\%, and a specific-heat jump that confirms a bulk pairing transition. All crystals show besides superconductivity a coexistence with a density-wave or metal-insulator transition. The upper critical field shows a small anisotropy, $γ\approx 2.4$, which remains finite as $T \to T_c$, indicating three-dimensional superconductivity with substantial coupling between the four-layer blocks. These results identify the square-planar nickelates $R_{n+1}$Ni$_n$O$_{2n+2}$ as a bulk platform in which the layer number alone tunes the nickel valence into the superconducting regime, without chemical substitution, pressure, or epitaxial constraint.

title: Structure-Informed Electromagnetic Feedback Control of the Vlasov-Maxwell System with Delayed Observations
summary: Feedback control of kinetic plasma instabilities is challenging because observing the full phase-space distribution is costly, while sensing and actuation inevitably introduce delay. We develop a structure-informed electromagnetic feedback framework for the Vlasov-Maxwell system that uses only macroscopic observations to control the full kinetic distribution. We first show that magnetic actuation alone does not directly regulate radial velocity moments, motivating the use of combined electric and magnetic controls. A nonlinear perturbation estimate yields an instantaneous cancellation-dissipation feedback law. To account for delayed observations, we then use Maxwell's equations to identify the macroscopic quantities governing the resulting cancellation errors, namely currents and spatial field gradients. These quantities serve as inputs to a low-rank neural operator that learns a residual correction to the delayed cancellation baseline. Thus, while the feedback depends only on low-dimensional macroscopic observables, the control objective remains the stabilization of the full distribution toward a prescribed kinetic equilibrium. Numerical experiments for two-stream and Weibel-type instabilities demonstrate effective long-time stabilization under substantial feedback delays.

title: Operator Learning of Microstructure-Dependent Internal-Variable Models for Inelastic Homogenization: Approximation and Complexity
summary: We study the learning of homogenized constitutive laws for inelastic heterogeneous materials, aiming to replace costly concurrent unit-cell simulations with surrogates that generalize across loading histories and microstructures. We focus on the recurrent neural operator framework, motivated by the explicit form of homogenized Kelvin--Voigt linear viscoelasticity. In this framework, internal variables enable a Markovian approximation of loading-history dependence, and neural operators represent the microstructure-dependent constitutive response. For periodic Kelvin--Voigt viscoelasticity, we prove a universal approximation theorem showing that the model can approximate the homogenized constitutive law to any prescribed accuracy, uniformly in time and over a wide set of admissible strain trajectories and microstructural property fields, in two and three dimensions. This comprises a significant extension of the existing, somewhat limited, one-dimensional theory that uses explicit solutions for piecewise constant materials. Instead, in two and three dimensions, we adopt a more versatile approximation based on the spectral representation of the memory kernel that arises from homogenization. This also enables us to give an explicit bound on the internal-variable dimension, sufficient for approximation, exhibiting logarithmic growth in the inverse relative stress error and in material contrast. Numerical experiments on viscoelasticity and crystal plasticity complement the theory, illustrating the roles of internal-variable dimension and sample complexity in learning homogenized responses from unit-cell data. Theoretical results are formally verified in Lean 4.

title: A Finite-Lag Markov Chain Model for Coarse-Graining Linear SDEs
summary: In this paper, we analyze a finite-lag Markov chain approximation for coarse-grained linear stochastic differential equations. The chain uses the limiting conditional transition law of the resolved variables to advance on a prescribed time grid. Its stability and statistical properties are studied, with particular attention to the role of the lag time. The chain preserves the exact equilibrium distribution and matches the autocovariance at the chosen lag, while errors at subsequent times are quantified. For a slow-fast system, the analysis relates lag selection to scale separation and dynamical accuracy. A continuous embedding of the chain enables a unified comparison with some existing continuous-time Markovian effective models based on the temporal statistics they preserve. Numerical examples illustrate the theoretical results.

title: Low-rank Low Precision Training of Gaussian Processes
summary: Training Gaussian processes (GPs) at large scale is computationally challenging because evaluating the log-marginal likelihood and its gradients involves large, dense kernel matrices. We develop a scalable low-rank GP training approach that combines AnchorNet landmark selection with a fully independent training conditional (FITC) correction. The resulting objective and its analytic gradients can be evaluated using low-rank factors, diagonal quantities, and small dense matrices, without forming the full kernel matrix or its derivatives. The complete training procedure is implemented in single precision and evaluated on nine large-scale regression datasets. Across these problems, the method reaches the reference predictive accuracy while substantially reducing training time, although the required approximation rank varies across datasets. We also study the numerical behavior of the full-kernel predictive solve and show that single precision can become limiting for ill-conditioned problems. Finally, we investigate further reducing selected matrix operations to fp16 or TF32. These lower-precision variants provide only modest additional speedups and can become unreliable when the reduced system is poorly conditioned.

title: A Computational Brainsphere Model for the Simulation of Alzheimer's Disease
summary:
Nowadays, there are different medical imaging techniques to collect data about the progression of
  Alzhei\-mer's disease in a patient's brain. These data describe different phenomena which are still
  not understood from a biological point of view.
  How can these data sets be combined in a mathematical model to simulate the evolution of such a
  neurodegenerative disease in a computer?
  In this snapshot, we present one possible approach to address this task with the help of graph theory
  and partial differential equations.

title: Convergence of finite element exterior calculus for the Hodge-Dirac and Hodge-Laplace problems on closed Riemannian manifolds
summary: We prove that the finite element exterior calculus (FEEC) approximation to the Hodge-Dirac and Hodge-Laplace problems on any closed oriented Riemannian manifold converges. Its approximate solutions, together with their exterior derivatives, converge to the continuum solutions for every source, and at the rate of the mesh size when the source and its codifferential are square integrable. We use Licht's estimate for the FEEC approximation of forms with one square-integrable derivative by finite element forms. We combine this with a new abstract error bound for approximations of Hilbert complexes. This bound uses a version of Di Pietro and Droniou's third Strang lemma. To apply these estimates, we show that every closed manifold admits a family of arbitrarily fine triangulations whose shapes stay uniformly under control.

title: Involution-Preserving schemes through constrained mesh motion: a novel Arbitrary-Lagrangian-Eulerian framework
summary: We introduce a novel structure-preserving finite volume method that exploits mesh motion to enforce differential involutions arising in hyperbolic systems of conservation laws. The key idea is to leverage the geometric degrees of freedom of an Arbitrary-Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) framework to construct a constrained mesh motion that is intrinsically compatible with the involution constraints embedded in the governing equations. The method is developed within a cell-centered formulation on moving quadrilateral meshes, where discrete divergence and curl operators are constructed from vertex-based differential operators. Particular care is devoted to the consistent evolution of the mesh geometry and the satisfaction of the Geometric Conservation Law (GCL). The proposed framework is applied to two representative hyperbolic systems featuring distinct involution constraints: the ideal magnetohydrodynamics equations, endowed with the divergence-free condition on the magnetic field, and the hyperbolic Euler-Heat equations, subject to a curl-free constraint on the thermal impulse. Second-order accuracy in time is achieved through a Runge-Kutta discretization, with the geometric constraints consistently enforced at each stage. A comprehensive set of classical benchmark problems is presented to assess the accuracy and effectiveness of the method. The numerical results demonstrate that appropriately constrained mesh motion provides an effective mechanism for preserving differential involutions, establishing a novel connection between mesh geometry and the structure-preserving discretization of hyperbolic systems.

title: Unmasking shortcut solutions of coding agents on partial differential equations
summary: Coding agents now write simulation programs, but benchmarks usually judge only whether their output matches a reference. In manufactured-solution tasks the data determine the exact solution, so a matching output need not come from a solver. We introduce PDEViBench, a benchmark of 290 tasks in six equation families that traces each passing program to the computation behind its output and reruns unclear programs on changed data. A Codex agent (GPT-5.2) passed 80% of 1,450 runs, yet about one pass in ten returned the exact solution without solving the equation. Counting only solved passes changed which task features made problems seem hard and reversed the ranking of two prompts. Once the prompt forbade the shortcut, every pass was a numerical solve, and on tasks without a closed-form solution passing programs stayed correct on changed data. Scientific coding benchmarks should check how each answer was computed as well as whether it matches.

title: Reconstructing Flash-Evoked Potentials in the Human Brain and Tracking Cortical Activity Using Spatiotemporal Filtering: Numerical Simulation Study
summary: Electroencephalographic source reconstruction of visual evoked activity is challenging because distributed, temporally evolving, and overlapping cortical sources generate scalp potentials. We present a controlled simulation framework for flash visual evoked potentials (FVEPs) based on a coupled Jansen--Rit neural mass network and a realistic finite-element EEG forward model. The framework generates a sequential activation pattern across early visual, parietal, and frontal regions and enables direct comparison of reconstructed activity with known ground truth. Standardized Kalman filtering (SKF), change-rate SKF (CrSKF), conventional Kalman filtering (KF), and linearly constrained minimum variance (LCMV) beamforming are compared using parcel-wise time courses, temporal lags, and assessments of spatial focality and Earth Mover's Distance. In the inverse comparison, SKF and CrSKF preserve the principal temporal progression more consistently than KF and LCMV, while CrSKF produces smoother temporal estimates. The results also demonstrate parcel-wise leakage and reduced separation of closely spaced components, emphasizing the need to interpret temporal ordering together with spatial reconstruction quality. The proposed framework provides a reproducible test environment for evaluating dynamic EEG inverse methods under controlled noise conditions.

title: Total variation error bounds for Schrödinger-Föllmer samplers
summary: Sampling from high-dimensional, multimodal target distributions plays a fundamental role in scientific computing, statistics and machine learning. Recently, the Schrödinger-Föllmer sampler (SFS) has been proposed by Huang et al. (IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory, 2025) as an efficient sampling algorithm that transports the degenerate distribution at $t=0$ to the target distribution at $t=1$, without relying on long-time ergodicity. In this paper, we establish non-asymptotic error bounds for SFS in the total variation distance by deriving regularization estimates for the associated Kolmogorov equation via the Bismut-Elworthy-Li formula. When the drift can be computed exactly, a convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}( h|\ln h|)$ was obtained under certain smoothness conditions on the drift with a uniform time step-size $h>0$. When the drift is approximated by Monte Carlo methods, we obtain a convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}( h|\ln h|+ 1/M)$, where $M$ is the number of samples used in the Monte Carlo approximation. This yields a sharper dependence on $M$ than the existing bound $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{M})$ in the $L^2$-Wasserstein distance in the aforementioned paper, by turning the total variation error to the weak error analysis in the setting of non-smooth test functions. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the convergence rate with respect to the time step-size $h$ and the Monte Carlo sample size $M$ and the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

title: VEM-bubble discretisation and iterative coupling algorithm for a fluid induced seismicity model with rate-and-state friction
summary: This work addresses the discretisation and iterative coupling algorithm for an induced seismicity model accounting for fault reactivation and slip driven by subsurface fluid injection. The model couples single-phase Darcy flow in both the porous matrix and the fault network with a quasi-static poroelastic mechanical response in the bulk and fault slip governed by a rate-and-state friction law with radiation damping stabilisation leading to a quas-dynamic formulation. The contact mechanics problem is discretised using the Virtual Element Method with bubble stabilisation of the facewise constant Lagrange multiplier. It is combined with a Hybrid Finite Volume scheme for the mixed-dimensional Darcy flow model. The time discretisation is implicit and the nonlinear system is solved at each time step using an iterative coupling algorithm which iterates between the Darcy flow, the frictional contact-mechanics, and the state differential equation. The contraction of this iterative coupling algorithm is established with a smallness assumption on the time step independent on the mesh size. This proves convergence of the fixed-point as well as well-posedness of the system. The frictional contact-mechanical model is solved using a semi-smooth Newton algorithm based on a local nonlinear inversion of the friction rate-and-state law and a block Gauss--Seidel preconditioner exploiting the structure of the VEM-bubble-$\mathbb{P}^0$ mixed discretisation.

title: An approximation for solutions to Helmholtz equation in polygons and its application in learning based numerical method
summary: A learning based method for Helmholtz equations was proposed in [J. Comput. Phys. 520:113478,2025]. Based on Runge's approximation, it can be proved that when the solution can be continued outside the computational domain, using fundamental solutions as learning samples is sufficient to obtain the solution mapping with spectral accuracy. However, for complex geometries, such as domains with corners, approximation by fundamental solutions may only have logarithmic convergence due to the regularity issue, which is computationally impracticable. Moreover, approximation of a solution to the elliptic equation with those on larger domains is an ill-posed problem. In this work, we investigate how to feed additional learning samples to essentially get a practicable convergence rate and a stable algorithm, so as to ensure the generalizability of the learning based method. Error analysis and numerical examples illustrate flexibility and high-accuracy features.

title: Investigating parameter dependence for counterexamples to Payne's nodal line conjecture using HPC
summary: The behavior of the nodal line of the second eigenfunction of the negative Laplacian has been widely studied. Dahne could show numerically for one domain with six holes in two dimensions that it is possible to reject Payne's nodal line conjecture. We investigate the behavior of the nodal line if it does not touch the boundary, specifically the general shape, its prediction, its dependence on the parameters, and the numbers of holes. In this paper, we could address these issues numerically with a very efficient parallelized algorithm showing the rejection for various domains with six and five holes.

title: A Large Gap between Galerkin Errors with and without Mesh-Uniform Regularity for the KdV Equation with Boundary Dissipation
comment: 44 pages, 2 figures. Ancillary files: the Lean 4 development for Theorem 3.1, and the programs, outputs and logs of the computations
summary: We compare two cubic Hermite Galerkin semidiscretizations of the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation. They use the same trial space. The first is the weighted scheme considered in our previous paper (arXiv:2610.39269), called the W-scheme. It has mesh-uniform regularity: the discrete semigroups of the linearized equation inherit Crandall-Pazy regularity and Kato smoothing, with bounds uniform in the mesh size $h$. The second is the standard Galerkin method in $L^2$, called the S-scheme. It has no mesh-uniform regularity. For the W-scheme, the full error and the ordering error converge at an algebraic rate in $h$, uniformly on $[t_0,\infty)$ times small balls of $L^2$ for any fixed $t_0>0$. They are bounded by $Ch^p\varepsilon$ and $Ch^p\varepsilon^2$, respectively, where $\varepsilon$ is the size of the datum and $p>0$. We prove that neither bound holds for the S-scheme by using exact high-frequency spurious eigenpairs of the S-scheme. The existence of such eigenpairs for fine meshes with at least 512 elements has a proof checked by Lean 4. Computations compare the two schemes on unit-norm data built from these eigenfunctions, on 512, 1024 and 2048 elements. The full error of the S-scheme stays at $4.6\times10^{-2}$. That of the W-scheme is at most $2.2\times10^{-9}$. The ordering error of the S-scheme stays at $9.6\times10^{-6}$. That of the W-scheme falls from $2.3\times10^{-9}$ to $1.4\times10^{-10}$. Their ratio grows from $4.2\times10^3$ to $6.6\times10^4$.

title: Shape Holomorphy of the Calderón Projector on Lipschitz Surfaces: Frequency-Explicit Bounds for the Helmholtz
summary:
We establish the holomorphic dependence of the Calderón projector for the Helmholtz operator upon shape boundary deformations of a family of bounded Lipschitz domains in two and three spatial dimensions, with bounds explicit in the wavenumber and the size of the holomorphic extension. More precisely, after transporting the four boundary integral operators contained in the Calderón projector to a fixed reference boundary, we prove that the resulting parameter-to-operator maps admit bounded holomorphic extensions in their natural fractional Sobolev spaces. Unlike approaches that require boundary regularity of class $\mathscr C^{1,1}$ or higher, our argument traces the holomorphic dependence on the shape by transferring elliptic estimates to the boundary through the fundamental solution and the Dirichlet and conormal trace operators. This construction is the key step that allows us to treat Lipschitz-regular boundary deformations.
  Furthermore, we show that the domain of holomorphy can be chosen independently of the wavenumber $κ$, while the operator bounds in the corresponding fractional Sobolev spaces contain algebraic factors in $κ$ multiplied by $\exp(Cκδ)$. In particular, for real domains, corresponding to $δ=0$, our single layer estimate recovers, to our knowledge, the best available frequency dependence on general Lipschitz boundaries. For the double layer, adjoint double layer, and hypersingular operators, we obtain novel frequency-explicit bounds.
  The results proved in this work provide the analytic foundation for frequency-explicit uncertainty quantification, model order reduction, and high-dimensional approximation of boundary integral operators, their Galerkin discretizations, and the resulting boundary densities and quantities of interest on families of parametrically varying boundaries.

title: Stochastic Multilevel Sampling for Inverse Problems via Coarse-Space Identifiability
summary: Sampling only part of the data reduces the cost of each iteration in an inverse problem, but can make reconstruction updates unreliable. We study stochastic multilevel sampling, which computes updates on a coarse-to-fine hierarchy of correction spaces. The guiding idea is that a small sample may support a reliable coarse-grid update even when it provides insufficient information for a fine-grid update. For quadratic objectives, we identify conditions under which corrections computed from sampled data decrease the full-data objective. In small-batch experiments with computed tomography and periodic deblurring, the stochastic multilevel method improves reconstruction accuracy over matched single-level methods. In an increasingly ill-conditioned CT refinement with a fixed number of projection angles, the single-level error increases as the image dimension grows, whereas a deep hierarchy maintains or improves accuracy and outperforms full-data single-level optimization at the same number of forward and adjoint applications. The gains persist across the tested local solvers and strengthen with deeper hierarchies. A separate known-probe ptychography study provides complementary evidence for the benefit of hierarchical corrections for nonlinear inverse problems.
